basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 31.' and it opens 'Vers. 31. Vocatus est locus Bersabee. Puteus Septimus, propter sex agnas quae ibi'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 31. Vocatus est locus Bersabee. Puteus Septimus, propter sex agnas quae ibi immolatae sunt. Vel puteus Juramenti, quia uterque ibi juraverat. Sabee utrumque sonat, et septem et juramentum. Hoc loco quaerendum quid sit quod superius legitur Agar stetisse ad puteum juramenti quod postea longo tempore factum est. Necdum enim ita vocabatur. Ergo per prolepsin, id est per praeoccupationem accipiendum | est: qui modus locutionis usitatissimus est in divinis Scripturis, quamvis potuerit esse illo tempore jam puteus. Quod si ita est, tunc per recapitulationem locus iste accipiendus est.
